meaning: Engulf weather reading: each day's forecast against past years, and what it means.
lead: 12 days away. Forecasts this far ahead are rough, so treat these as best guesses. This page updates twice a day.
banner: This is preliminary until about Nov 7, when the hour-by-hour forecast for burn night comes in. It gets more accurate the closer we get to the burn.
summary: Right now the forecasts point to afternoons around 70°, nights around 49°, and a chance of a shower or two.
Burn night looks like light wind (around 5 mph), probably dry, and about 54° at the burns.
NOAA's longer-range outlook for Nov 7–13 leans slightly warmer than normal, with rain about normal. It gives odds for the whole stretch, not a forecast for any one day.
The last 30 days ran warm and dry: highs about 4° above normal, and 1.9 of a usual 3.5 inches of rain at McComb. The parish is in drought, so the ground is dry and burn bans are possible.
In a normal Engulf week, afternoons run around 72° and nights around 45°; it rains on about 1 in 7 days, frost comes about 1 in 10 nights, and wind at burn time rarely reaches 15 mph.

When you'll know more: the European forecast reaches burn night in the next day or two; the hour-by-hour forecast for burn night starts around Nov 7; from about Nov 11, three days out, forecasts are usually within a few degrees.
